purpose: Department voices from the Four-Axis Voice and Bias Matrix (Mystery Engine Design Research, Track 6). Profiles are keyed by style, not by department name (project decision, Entry 024): the seed sampler assigns one profile to each department slot and S2 maps the case's real departments onto those slots. Findings are always plain; a profile governs the assessment section and any document the department authors. Exemplars are nonsense and show syntax only.
source: Mystery Engine Design Research, Track 6, 'Character Voice Differentiation, Detectable Bias, and Unreliable Testimony'. The research names example departments (records, signal, optics, assay); here they are only sources, not keys.

axes.name: lens
axes.meaning: how the bias colours an assessment

axes.name: tell
axes.meaning: how a careful player detects the bias

position.AX-1: clipped telegraphic clauses, passive verbs, numbers always in digits, probability brackets
position.AX-2: every anomaly is deliberate; nobody is ever merely careless
position.AX-3: reads an erased line, a typo or a late entry as premeditated
position.AX-4: attaches precise probabilities of intent to mundane irregularities that other documents explain as petty and human

exemplars: Line 4 of FIXTURE-R2 erased. Erasure assessed deliberate. [Probability 91%.] Entry FIXTURE-03 re-written at 16:42.
Two seals on FIXTURE-07 replaced in 1 shift. Replacement pattern assessed intentional. [Probability 87%.]

position.AX-1: rhythmic, sensory prose about cadence, breath, room sound and emotional subtext
position.AX-2: trusts the sound of sincerity over records and rank
position.AX-3: defends a speaker who sounds frightened or grieving, even when their facts are wrong
position.AX-4: excuses a spoken claim as strain while faithfully bracketing the background sound that contradicts it

profiles.bias: A sincere-sounding voice is believed over the record.
exemplars: The speaker in FIXTURE-09 slows on every third phrase, a cadence that seems to me the strain of someone tired rather than someone hiding, and I would not read the pause as anything more.
There is a held breath before the reply in FIXTURE-11 that likely reflects grief, and the voice stays level and sincere even where the account wanders.

position.AX-1: hyper-precise geometric and material description, positions and measurements, no emotional adjectives
position.AX-2: only what an instrument records is real; testimony and rank are noise
position.AX-3: fixes on the prominent physical subject and treats human use of the space as irrelevant
position.AX-4: lists every object in the frame with the same neutrality, so the decisive background item is there for the player to notice

profiles.bias: Only recorded physical evidence counts; human context is dismissed.
exemplars: Foreground: FIXTURE-05 lies at 30 degrees to the bench edge, 412 mm from the left upright. Background, upper right quadrant: 2 cups, 1 cloth, non-structural.
The panel in FIXTURE-08 shows 3 parallel marks, 14 mm apart, left of centre. Testimony regarding use of the room is not relevant to the frame.

position.AX-1: formal academic prose, long subordinate clauses, deference to hierarchy and protocol
position.AX-2: loyal to senior people and the institution's reputation; blames outsiders and juniors
position.AX-3: interprets residue and records in ways that protect senior staff and flagship work
position.AX-4: uses deferential hedging immediately after logging a finding that implicates someone senior

profiles.bias: Senior people and the institution are protected; juniors and outsiders are blamed.
exemplars: Given the long standing of the senior officer named in FIXTURE-R4, we consider it far more likely that the material was obtained through unauthorised borrowing by junior staff than that it was used by its registered holder.

While the match recorded in FIXTURE-06 is clear, we would suggest that protocol was most probably breached by a visitor, since nothing in the senior team's conduct to date would support a different reading.
